 Judgment

This reference filed by the petitioner - SLAO under Sections 30 and 31 of KIADB Act, 1966 read with Section 151 of CPC, seeking permission to deposit the compensation amount for the acquired land and for adjudication on the rightful recipient of the award amount deposited by the petitioner.

.2. The case made out by the petitioner in nutshell is that the petitioner for the purpose of development by the KIADB issued a Preliminary Notification under Section 28(1) bearing No.
CI/108/SPQ/2015 dated 21/22.09.2015 in respect of acquired property and other properties and Final Notification has been issued under Section 28(4) of KIAD Act bearing No. CI/108/SPQ/2015 dated 22.02.2018.

It is further claimed by the petitioner L.A.C. No.74/2022 that the respondent filed W.P.No. 24533- 24534/2017, 25334/2017 C.W. No.24535- 24536/2017, 25877-25880/2017 and the said Writ Petitions came to be disposed off in terms of the order dated 21.11.2017.

Wherein,
the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka was pleased to direct the SLAO, KIADB to refer the dispute under Sections 30 and 31 of L.A. Act to reference Court, the applicant passed an order bearing No.
KIADB/METRO/AWARD/394/2018-19 dated 11.09.2018 to deposit the compensation amount before this Court referring the matter to decide the issue in question.
Accordingly, the petitioner filed this reference before this Court for respective prayers stated therein.

.3. The claimant N. Revathi has filed claim statement, wherein, she admitted about issuance of Preliminary Notification and Final Notification for acquisition of acquired land and claimed that the fair market value of the sites sold in the schedule property is around Rs.8,100/- per Sq. feet and L.A.C. No.74/2022 accordingly, they have negotiated for paying the market value of the sites at the rate of Rs.16,000/- and they are entitled for compensation under the new LA Act, 2013.
The officials of the Government who were involved in the process of land acquisition and payment of the compensation, delayed the process of payment of compensation.

Hence, a suo-moto proceedings is initiated by the Assistant Commissioner, Bengaluru South Sub Division, Bengaluru and passed the impugned order dated 26.05.2017 without issuing the notices to the interested persons.
Hence, the said order has been challenged in W.P.No. 25877/2017 and connected matters.

Accordingly, the impugned order dated 26.05.2017 passed by the Assistant Commissioner in case No.
LND/RA(S)18/2016-17 was quashed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka as per final order dated 07.02.2022.

As per the order of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P.No. 25877/2017 and connected L.A.C. No.74/2022 matters, the Hon'ble High Court has to decide the person who is entitled for compensation.

.4. Claimant also claimed that the property bearing No. 87 was Government land out of which an extent of 2.10 guntas was granted in favour of one Ramaiah during the year 1927 and the khatha was also changed to his name in view of the grant.

The said Ramaiah died on 04.07.1938 leaving behind him, his wife and children and they have partitioned the properties as per partition deed dated 29.06.1974 vide registration No. 6328/1974- The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State, Revenue Department on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135161528/
2 75.

sentences.text: In the said partition, the property in Sy. No. 87/2 measuring 2.10 acres allotted to the share of Gowramma.
The said Gowramma died intestate leaving behind her, her children namely Rangaswamy, Somashekar, Ramakrishna and Savithri as surviving legal heirs.

.5. Claimant claimed that meantime the property bearing Sy. No. 87/2 was acquired for benefit of BDA under Preliminary Notification under Section 17(1) of the B.D.A. Act dated 23.03.1988 L.A.C.
No.74/2022 followed by Final Notification under Section 19(1) of the B.D.A. Act dated 19.10.1994.

The said acquisition proceedings and Final Notification have been challenged in W.P.No.
31892/2009 and connected matters.

In the said matters, issue was raised as to whether the Sy. No.
87 was the Government land or not.
In the said writ petition, the B.D.A. claimed that the property in Sy. No. 87 was a Government land.
Meantime, the B.D.A. wanted to ascertain the details of the grants made in Sy. No. 87 and accordingly, the matter has been referred to the Deputy Commissioner, Bengaluru Urban District, Bengaluru.

In view of the said letter from the B.D.A., the Special Deputy Commissioner initiated the proceedings by directing the Special Tahsildar,
Bengaluru South Taluka to make an inquiry as to auctions and the grants made in Sy. No. 87 and to furnish the details.

The Special Tahsildar has initiated the proceedings and after holding an inquiry,
filed report dated 05.04.2005 to the Special Deputy Commissioner along with index L.A.C.
No.74/2022 of land, Mysore Revision settlement Register etc., which shows the allotment of property to various persons.
.6.

Claimant claimed that in inquiry proceedings in RRT (North) CR-16/2005-06, Smt. Saraswathi appeared before the Deputy Tahsildar and filed certain documents including Manjuri- Hukum dated 05.07.1929, partition deed dated 29.06.1974 and mutation is also made out in MR No. 114/2004-05 and given a finding that the property originally granted to Ramaiah.

It is further stated that the said property has been conveyed in favour of Smt. Revathi N, Rekha N, Damodhara and N.
Chandrashekar under a registered sale deed dated 12.09.2009.
The said Developer had developed the said property in the name and style of Classic Orchards Phase-III layout and various sites were sold in favour of subsequent purchasers.
The claimant is one of the purchasers of such sites formed.
The claimant specifically claimed that she has purchased the site No. 108 measuring 2700 Sq. feet in the aforesaid layout under a registered sale deed dated 05.03.2015.
As per the said sale deed, the market value of the property is Rs. 7,407/- per Sq. feet and the market value of the property as on 05.03.2015 was Rs. 7,896/- per Sq. feet.

Further stated that the market value of the property has been increased to Rs. 8,848/- per Sq. feet as per sale deed dated 7.11.2017 and also stated that the claimant is entitled for compensation at rate of Rs. 20,574/- per Sq. feet in respect of plot No.34.

Accordingly, prayed to allow the claim of claimant.
.8.

The respondent No. 2 BMRCL has filed objections stating that the beneficiary of acquisition BMRCL sent a compensation package to the Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB, fixing the market value at Rs.44,046/- per sq. meters through letter dated 30.07.2018.
It is stated that after receipt of compensation package from BMRCL, Special Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB issued notice under L.A.C. No.74/2022 Section 29(2) to the Khatedars.
During inquiry the SLAO noticed that there existed W.P. No. 24533- 24534/2017.

It is stated that W.P. No. 25334- 25335/2017 and W.P. No. 25877-25880/2017 pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in-respect of the The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State, Revenue Department on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135161528/
3 property in question.

sentences.text: In view of the same, the SLAO could not take decision regarding ownership and apportionment of compensation.

Hence, he proceeded to pass General Award and also deposited the compensation package into the Civil Court and referred the matter to the Court under Section 30 and 31 of L.A. Act, for disbursement of compensation after determining the rights of the parties.

It is stated that the respondent No. 2 BMRCL who is beneficiary of acquisition will not be liable to pay interest on the awarded compensation amount as also held in the decision 1995(5) SCC 577 (SLAO Vs. Puttaiah and others).
.9.
In order to prove claimant's case, the GPA holder of claimant namely M.V. Ramaswamy Raju L.A.C. No.74/2022 is examined as PW.1.

The documents got marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12.
.10.

On the basis of the above, the point for consideration is that:
"Whether the claimant is entitled to receive the compensation amount in this case?"
.11.
Heard the arguments.

Perused the materials on record, on that basis my finding on the above point is in the affirmative, for the following:
REASONS .12. Point No.1:
This reference has been referred to this Court under Section 29 of the KIADB Act, to decide the rightful recipient of the award amount deposited by the petitioner.

In the case on hand, it is undisputed fact that the schedule property has been acquired under Preliminary Notification dated 22.09.2015 and Final Notification dated 22.02.2018 and General Award passed on 11.09.2018.

It is also admitted fact in this case that the respondent has filed W.P.No.
24533- L.A.C. No.74/2022 534/2017, W.P.No.25334-25335/17 and W.P.No. 25877-880/2017, that have been disposed off on 21.11.2017.
Thereafter, Final Notification has been issued and the award has been passed.

Subsequently, the petitioner deposited a sum of Rs.39,14,942/- out of Rs. 48,93,678/-
claiming that they have deducted 20% towards income tax.
.13. As discussed earlier, the reference is made to the Court and the amount has been deposited to the Court by the petitioner in order to decide the rightful recipient of the award amount.
Hence, the Court has to give a specific finding that who is the owner of the acquired land as described in the schedule property.
In the case on hand, the claimant Smt. Revathi claimed that she is the absolute owner of the schedule property.

The claim of the claimant is that the property bearing Sy. No. 87 was Government land, out of which, an extent of 2 acres 10 guntas of land was granted in favour of Ramaiah during the year 1927 and accordingly, the khatha has been changed in his name.
L.A.C. No.74/2022
Subsequently after the death of said Ramaiah, his surviving LRs have entered into the partition deed dated 29.06.1974 and in the said partition, the guntas of land allotted to the share of Gowramma.

After the death of Gowramma, her children namely Rangaswamy,
Somashekar, Ramakrishna and Savithri succeeded to the said property and thereafter, as per the Preliminary Notification issued by the B.D.A. dated 23.03.1988 followed by Final Notification dated The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State, Revenue Department on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135161528/
4 19.10.1994.

sentences.text: The said property has been acquired by the B.D.A., and the same has been challenged in W.P.No. 31892/2009 and connected cases.
Subsequently, there is dispute regarding extent of grant of the land and inquiry has been held in RRT (North)CR-16/2005- 06.

Wherein, it is held that the property originally granted to Ramaiah and in the said proceedings,
it is also held that the property has been conveyed in favour of Smt. Revathi, N Rekha, N.
Damodhara L.A.C. No.74/2022 and N. Chandrashekar under a registered sale deed dated 12.11.2009.
.14.

The property involved in this case is described in acquired land at Sl. No.9 of the notification No.CI/108/SPQ/2015, Bengaluru dated 21/22.09.2015 as described as DP-1/A Plot No.34 in Sy.
No.87 measuring 111.41 Sq. Meters and that has been also described in the general award dated 11.09.2018.
.15.

In the case on hand, the claimant in the claim statement prayed for enhancement of compensation, but this reference is not for determining the market value of the properties but only to decide the title of claimant over the acquired property.
Hence, the claim of claimant for enhancement of market value or determination of market value of the acquired property is not considered.

.16. In the case on hand, the ownership of Smt. Revathi over the aforesaid property involved in this case is not in dispute and the Competent L.A.C. No.74/2022 Revenue Authorities in full pledged inquiry held that they have acquired valid right, title and interest over the property.
The said Smt Revathi and others purchased the property under a registered sale deed dated 12.11.2009 as per Ex.P.6.

As per the said document, surviving LRs of Gowramma jointly sold the property to Smt.
Revathi and others.

Therefore, the oral and documentary evidence produced before the Court sufficiently shows that the claimant is the absolute owner of the acquired property and claimant is entitled for the compensation.

Accordingly, the above point is answered in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The reference made under Sections 30 and 31(2) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 is hereby allowed.

Claimant N. Revathi is entitled to receive the compensation in respect of the land bearing Identification No.R6-  L.A.C. No.74/2022  DP1/A Plot No.34 in Sy. No.87  measuring 111.41 Sq. Meters of  Kothanur village, Bangaluru South Taluka along with statutory benefits.

The claimant shall has to execute an indemnity bond with one surety, undertaking to re-deposit the compensation amount either in The Special Land Acquisition ... vs The State, Revenue Department on 6 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135161528/
